episode_title: How This Agency Owner Freed Up 5 Hours a Week in Just 7 Days w/ Gabriela Krawczyk

real_qa.q: How much time did Gabriela Krawczyk free up in the first 7 days of the FreeUp Founder Challenge?
real_qa.r: In the first seven days of completing the FreeUp Founder Challenge, Gabriela was able to free up five hours per week of time that was going into reactive work, such as responding to messages, emails, or admin work that could be scheduled later in the day. This allowed her to protect the first two hours of every day, Monday through Friday.
real_qa.requete: FreeUp Founder Challenge results Gabriela Krawczyk

real_qa.q: What is the hourly wage bleed concept mentioned in the FreeUp Founder time audit?
real_qa.r: The hourly wage bleed is about putting a dollar amount to the time spent on something that can be eliminated, delegated, or automated. It makes the abstract concept of 'time is money' concrete and actionable. By calculating this, agency owners can identify work that takes away from their highest-value activities and determine what should be eliminated, delegated, or automated to maximize time spent on work that generates value.

real_qa.q: What specific mindset shift did Gabriela Krawczyk have about client response times during the FreeUp Founder program?
real_qa.r: Gabriela realized that replying to client emails within five minutes does not align with what clients actually hired her for. She shifted her thinking to understand that clients hired her to do a specific job and help them grow their business, not just to be responsive. She implemented a 24-hour SLA for non-urgent requests, which is still acceptable, and now dedicates up to one hour per day to email triage and response.
real_qa.requete: client response time SLA agency owner

real_qa.q: What was the most impactful quick change Gabriela implemented for reducing distractions at Little Jack Marketing?
real_qa.r: Turning off all banner notifications on her desktop was described as mind-blowing in its impact for limiting distractions. Additionally, she removed social media apps (LinkedIn, Instagram, Reddit) from her phone so they can only be accessed on her desktop, making doom-scrolling much harder. During work hours, she sets her phone to sleep mode or do-not-disturb and intentionally checks apps during breaks.

real_qa.q: What are the four weeks of the FreeUp Founder challenge structured to accomplish according to Jesse Gilmore?
real_qa.r: Week one focuses on internal habits and emotional separation of founder from business. Week two builds those changes into client contracts with written boundaries. Week three eliminates non-value-added work like massive slide decks and monthly reporting. Week four establishes a rigid calendar schedule to sustain the changes beyond the challenge.

guest.bio_context: Gabriela Krawczyk is the managing partner of Little Jack Marketing, a small agency working with small business owners. She recently joined the FreeUp Founder program and completed the first seven-day challenge, freeing up five hours per week of reactive work. She has historical knowledge of her clients and has been the central bottleneck in client delivery, which motivated her to seek systematization and leadership evolution.
